concepts.def: Festival of breaking the fast — end of Ramadan
Shi'a day of mourning for Husayn at Karbala (680 CE)
Night of Power — Qur'an first revealed
Inner struggle to be a better Muslim
Defensive outer struggle, under strict rules

walkthroughs.body_html:
Eid al-Fitr celebrates the end of Ramadan — feasting, special prayer, new clothes, charity (Zakat al-Fitr).

Laylat al-Qadr — 'Night of Power' — falls in the last 10 nights of Ramadan and remembers when the Qur'an was first revealed to Muhammad through angel Jibril.

Surah 97 says it is 'better than a thousand months'.

Eid al-Adha — 'festival of sacrifice' — during Hajj. Remembers Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his son when commanded; Allah provided a ram instead.

Muslims who can afford it sacrifice an animal; meat is shared with family, friends and the poor.

Ashura (10th of Muharram) — Shi'a Muslims mourn the martyrdom of Husayn (Muhammad's grandson) at Karbala in 680 CE. Sunni Muslims may fast.

Jihad means 'to strive' — not 'holy war'.

Greater jihad: inner struggle to follow Allah — Muhammad called it the more important struggle.

Lesser jihad: outer struggle, allowed only in self-defence, with strict rules — no harming civilians, women, children, or trees. Mainstream Muslims reject terrorism — Qur'an 5:32 condemns killing the innocent.
